<thought>We need to determine how many methyl (CH₃) groups are present in the compound of the sample. The best way is to retrieve the 13C NMR spectrum for the sample, then count the number of signals in the typical methyl carbon region (around 10–30 ppm). This will give the number of distinct CH₃ carbons, which corresponds to the number of methyl groups. We'll request the carbon NMR spectrum.</thought>
